answer: The falcon multiplier is published, charged in onyx, and violet lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 12 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 812 identities would post 2270 proofs and burn roughly 15 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
